Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
350 PM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
An upper-low will meander offshore bringing light lowland rain 
and mountain snow to the area this weekend. The pattern becomes
more active next week as a series of systems brings widespread 
precipitation, gusty winds, and the increasing potential for 
coastal flooding.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TONIGHT THROUGH MONDAY NIGHT/...
A pattern change is beginning to unfold across the region as an
upper-low meanders offshore. It'll continue to spin periods of 
light lowland rain showers and light mountain snow into Sunday. 
A high center in northern BC is interacting with the 
aforementioned low, forming a blocking pattern leaving the 
upper-level progression rather stagnant for the next 24 to 30 
hours. It'll become ingested within the mean flow on Sunday 
night into early Monday morning as broad troughing envelopes 
the NE PAC. During this time precipitation is slated to become
steadier, starting over the Olympics before gradually spreading
inland. Snow levels will start off around 2,000-3,000 ft before
rising into the day on Monday. As a result, a Winter Weather
Advisory has been issued for the Olympics including Hurricane 
Ridge where 5-10" of snow is forecast throughout the duration of
this event. Transient ridging on Monday evening may allow a 
brief break in the action before the next front arrives late 
overnight into Tuesday. Temperatures in the short term near 
seasonal with highs in the upper 40s to lower 50s. Overnight 
lows are to be in the 30s to lower 40s.

Coastal Flooding: The next round of larger high tides, coupled 
with increased surge and wave action, will bring a return of 
coastal flood concerns to the Pacific Coast with Sunday's high 
tide. While conditions on the north coast are more marginal, 
confidence is sufficiently high to warrant a high surf advisory 
for Sunday morning's high tide. Conditions will increase more 
sharply Monday onward, as larger waves and lower pressure may 
only combine to push water levels higher along the Pacific coast
through early part of next week.

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
The aforementioned upper-trough and it's associated low will 
then deepen offshore on Tuesday and will bring a more active 
pattern to western Washington as the system swings a number of 
disturbances across the region. Expect multiple rounds of 
widespread lowland rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds starting
Tuesday and persisting through the second half of the week. The
system moving across the area on Tuesday will also bring 
another round of high surf to the coast. Additionally, high 
astronomical tides combined with the weather impacts from these 
systems, will increase the threat for coastal flooding - most 
notably along the Pacific Coast during high surf.

Coastal Flooding: Confidence is increasing for the potential of
moderate to major coastal flooding stages being reached along 
portions of the Grays Harbor County coastline during the Tuesday
and Wednesday tides, and high surf may only enhance these 
impacts. The tides increase more significantly for the Strait 
and Puget Sound coastlines later in the week around Tuesday 
onward, and the potential for impacts in these locations will 
need to be closely monitored as we get into the range of total 
water level guidance.

&&

.AVIATION...
Variable flow aloft turning southeasterly this evening before
later southwesterly on Sunday as an upper-low meanders offshore. 
A mid-level cloud deck is expanding across the region as VFR 
conditions prevail. Light showers are also accompanying the
increasing clouds. Tonight, as showers progress ceilings will 
gradually lower to either a low-end VFR or MVFR level early 
Sunday morning, with the lowest ceilings in the south interior.
VFR conditions are to return by Sunday afternoon with lingering
shower activity. 


KSEA...VFR conditions at the terminal this evening. MVFR
ceilings are favored to return late tonight into early Sunday
morning. They'll remain in place before rising to VFR around
midday. Surface winds becoming SE tonight between 5-10 kt;
trending more southerly and lighter into Sunday. 

&&

.MARINE...
A passing system this evening will maintain advisory strength winds 
and steep, wind-driven seas over the coastal waters into early 
Sunday. Expect seas to build to around 12-14 ft by early Sunday with 
a westerly swell arriving. 

After this, a very active marine pattern will unfold with a strong 
low offshore sending a series of disturbances across the waters 
during much of the week ahead. Late Sunday will bring widespread 
advisory winds with some potential for low-end gale gusts tomorrow 
night into Monday. Ensemble guidance suggests a better chance of 
gales (40-60%) Monday night into Tuesday over the coastal waters, 
with a 30% chance of storm gusts over the outer coastal waters. Yet 
another disturbance follows late Wednesday with perhaps the best 
chance of seeing storm force winds over the outer coastal waters. 
Meanwhile, seas will build through the week with high confidence in 
seas above 16 ft Tuesday and Wednesday, and around a 40% chance of 
20 ft seas. Even if seas don't build this big, the dominant period 
will be rather long Tuesday and Wednesday, which will lead to 
confused seas as winds increase and mix this swell with shorter 
period, locally generated seas. Cullen

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Wetter systems moving into the region next week will start to
bring some rises to area rivers. At this time, no widespread river
flooding is expected, however the Skokomish River will likely
cross into minor flood stage minor flood stage around midweek
onward.
